name: Saw palmetto

lead: Saw palmetto (Serenoa repens) is a palm native to the south-eastern United States whose berry extract is sold as a supplement for prostate symptoms and hair loss. It is among the most common natural products promoted as a DHT blocker.
Trials in pattern hair loss are few, small and often of poor quality, and the results suggest an effect much smaller than that of finasteride. It is best viewed as preliminary-evidence.

paras: Extracts contain fatty acids and phytosterols that weakly inhibit 5-alpha-reductase in laboratory studies and may block androgen receptor binding. The inhibition measured in cells is far weaker than that of prescription drugs, and the clinical relevance is uncertain.

It is usually well tolerated, with mild stomach upset, headache and, occasionally, effects on hormone-sensitive conditions. It may interact with anticoagulants and hormonal medications and is not recommended in pregnancy. It is sold as an unregulated supplement, so potency varies between products.
